deities: Lord Krishna after Kamsavadham, in Raudra (ferocious) posture - main deity; food (nivedyam) is offered first thing on opening the sanctum since the Lord is believed hungry and tired after the battle
Goddess Durga (shrine in the middle of the temple tank; one of the 108 Durga temples of ancient Kerala; also identified as Loga-Maya)
Lord Shiva, Lord Ganesha, Sastha and Naga devatas (shrines in/near the complex)
festivals: Trichambaram Utsavam - 10-day annual festival from Kumbham 22 to Meenam 6 (February-March); Balarama image brought from the Mazhoor/Dharmakulangara temple; thidambu dance by priests, thidambu nritham, Arattu at the chira, and the farewell scene of Krishna and Balarama
Vishu, Onam, Navaratri (per one travel site - verify)

history.period: In existence in the 11th century CE - mentioned in the Sanskrit kavya Mushikavamsa; renovated several times; destroyed by invaders and renovated in the late 18th century
history.summary: One of Kerala's three best-known Krishna temples (with Guruvayur and Ambalappuzha), and called 'North Guruvayoor'. Legend credits Parasurama with the installation; the name 'Trichambaram' is linked to Sambara Maharshi, who is said to have performed tapas at the Sambaravanam forest here. The temple enshrines Krishna jubilant after slaying Kamsa - the deity sits in the ferocious Raudra aspect, tired and hungry from the battle with Kamsa's royal tusker Kuvalayapida, hence the unique ritual of feeding the Lord before other rites. Because Krishna slew the elephant Kuvalayapida, elephants are a taboo at this temple - uniquely, the utsava murti is carried on priests' heads instead. It was built soon after the Taliparamba Shiva temple to temper Siva's fierceness, per one guide. The small two-storeyed sanctum has 15th-16th century murals and carvings. CSV TOWN FLAG: the temple is NOT in Kannur town - it is at Trichambaram in Taliparamba, about 20 km north of Kannur. Documented with the corrected location.

name: Trichambaram Sree Krishna Temple
town: Taliparamba (CSV town 'Kannur' is the district HQ/city ~20 km away - corrected)
town_description: Trichambaram is in Taliparamba town, about 20 km north of Kannur on the banks of the Kuppam river, in Kannur district. The temple is about 1.5 km from Taliparamba town centre, on Parassini Road.

travel.railway: Kannur Railway Station - about 20 km; buses/taxis from Kannur.
travel.road: About 1.5 km from Taliparamba town; local buses, taxis and autos from Kannur and Taliparamba.

visitor_information.best_time: Kumbham (February-March) for the 10-day Trichambaram Utsavam; March is recommended by travel guides.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Reported as 5:00 AM - 12:00 noon and 5:00 PM - 8:00 PM daily (pilgrimaide, poojn.in); one source lists 5:30 AM - 12:00 PM and 5:00 - 8:30 PM (verify - confirm locally). Men must wear mundu and remove shirts; women traditional dress.
